meta.method: Opened and visually inspected 11 SIH PDFs from public GitHub archives (page images + text), read the SIH 2026 playbook PDF, and read three public pitch-craft sources (Sequoia template, Colosseum/DePitch slide-by-slide guide, a compiled investor-advice file citing YC/Hoffman/a16z/DocSend). WebSearch was unavailable; Bing/Brave via WebFetch returned almost no deck links (Brave rate-limited with 429).
caveats: RANKS ARE UNVERIFIED: the archives label files 'Winner' or '1st Prize' in filenames, but SIH has nodal-level, internal and Grand Finale winners and the repos do not say which. Treat 'winner' as 'labelled winner in a public archive'.

Most SIH decks are the official 6-slide idea-submission template (screening stage). They show what passes screening, not what wins a 10-minute pitch. They are weak on benchmarking, costs, revenue and market size, which are exactly MalanHack's pillars, so the synthesis leans on pitch-craft sources for those.

No public deck was found for RBI HaRBInger, SEBI TechSprint, Flipkart GRiD, HDFC/ICICI hackathons, Devpost, ETHGlobal or lablab winners. Repos found (e.g. HaRBInger entries, 'Hackathon Fight The Fraud' technical-prize winner, YC Locus 'Safepay') contain only code/READMEs, no slides. Airbnb/Uber decks are indexed in github.com/midovislam/awesome-pitch-decks (Google Drive links) but could not be downloaded here; Airbnb/Uber/LinkedIn/Coinbase/Square observations come from a secondary compilation, not from opening the PDFs.
Words-per-slide are estimates for image-only PDFs (counted from extracted text where available).

decks.title: ECommerce Dark Pattern Detector (Team AlgoAllies)
decks.first_3_slides: Title, team list, then a text-only problem statement. Problem is described in prose with no number, no source and no visual; the team slide takes the prime slot 2.
decks.architecture_visual: One small yellow-box step-by-step flowchart (about 14 boxes, tiny type) for the Chrome extension pipeline. Unreadable at projector size.
decks.numbers: None. No stats, no market size, no cost, no citations.
decks.stood_out: Cyber/consumer-protection domain match to LienLine. Distinctive full-bleed red brand with repeating team name. Weak on evidence; it is a negative example for problem rigour and numbers.

decks.title: greenSort AI (Team AKY)
slide_order: Idea title + problem resolution + unique value propositions
Impact and benefits (impact/benefit pairs + user-flow map)
decks.first_3_slides: Admin title page, then a dense idea slide with a named product and slogan, then tech logos + workflow diagram. Solution is stated before any problem evidence.
decks.architecture_visual: Logo wall grouped as Web / AI-ML / Additional, beside a boxed left-to-right workflow flowchart (upload image -> detect -> reward / communicate to vendor / municipality).
decks.numbers: Almost none ('2000+ images' only). No market or cost figures.
decks.demo_screenshots: None; a site map diagram stands in.
decks.stood_out: Risks and challenges paired with 'Solution' on the same slide, and a references slide with real data and tech links. Pattern to copy: every risk gets a mitigation.

decks.title: CIS-GPO Automator for Air-Gapped Security (Team Cannon Crew)
slide_order: Solution in three chevron columns (Detailed explanation / How it addresses the problem / Innovation and uniqueness)
Technical approach (architecture flowchart + component list + tech logos)
decks.first_3_slides: Title, then a 3-column 'what / how it solves / why unique' slide, then architecture. This is the cleanest slide 2 in the set: the argument is structured, not a paragraph.
decks.architecture_visual: Full-width multi-agent style flowchart (chain of LLM agents, FAISS RAG, script generator -> executor -> evaluator) with a bordered component glossary and a row of 8 logos (FastAPI, Mistral, Ollama, MongoDB, Electron, ChromaDB, PowerShell). Closest analogue to LienLine's multi-agent architecture; diagram text is too small.
decks.demo_screenshots: None; a concrete user-story scenario (agency with air-gapped network) replaces it.
decks.stood_out: Security-domain framing, offline/air-gapped constraint as differentiator, and a worked user story with Scenario -> Impact -> Benefits.

decks.title: Women Safety Analytics (Team Innovators)
slide_order: Proposed solution + 3 coloured boxes (problem / how it addresses / innovation) + stock imagery
Tech approach (language / framework / hardware boxes + alert flow)
Impact (for women / law enforcement / communities + social/economic/environmental)
decks.first_3_slides: Title, solution paragraph with campaign-style imagery, then a coloured-box tech and alert-flow diagram.
decks.architecture_visual: Loose boxes-and-arrows (App -> Police / Family / Friends alerts). Low rigour; text clipped at edges.
decks.stood_out: Stakeholder-segmented impact slide (who gains what). Visually inconsistent and clipped text; a reminder that content passes screening even with rough design, but would not stand out in a design-aware round.

decks.title: AlertMe: Emergency Response Coordination Platform (Team Techbyte)
slide_order: Objective + solution bullets + mind-map of 5 modules
decks.first_3_slides: Title, objective + named solution with a hub-and-spoke module map, then stack + build phases.
decks.architecture_visual: Hub-and-spoke mind map (Alert Me -> Data aggregation, Resource mgmt, Crowd source, Comms hub, Incident mgmt) plus a numbered 01-04 chevron build plan.
decks.demo_screenshots: None; a Figma prototype link is in references.
decks.stood_out: Viability slide separates market, social and partnership/funding lines, the only SIH deck here with a funding line (still unquantified).

decks.title: Rockfall Prediction and Alert System (Team GeoGuards)
decks.event: SIH 2025, Disaster Management and Mining Safety (SIH25071)
slide_order: Idea title: addressing the problem + solution overview (3 pills) + pit-mine cross-section image
Technical approach (vertical 5-step pipeline -> Low/Medium/High risk with sample charts)
Feasibility (4 pills) + pie chart of rockfall causes
decks.first_3_slides: Title, a short problem-to-solution slide anchored by a domain illustration, then a vertical step pipeline with real prediction charts.
decks.architecture_visual: Vertical numbered pipeline (Step I-V) fanning into three risk outcomes, with actual output charts on the right. Best 'show the output' architecture in the set.
decks.numbers: One pie chart of cause shares (15/20/25%...), no sourcing; otherwise none.
decks.demo_screenshots: No UI shots; model output charts act as proof.

decks.title: RockVision AI (Team Tech Pioneers)
decks.event: SIH 2025, Disaster Management and Mining Safety (SIH25071)
slide_order: Product name + proposed solution (7 bold-lead bullets) + system architecture diagram
Technical approach: categorised stack list + logo grid
Feasibility and viability + business potential (subscription, tiering, partnerships)
Impact: benefits tree + per-audience impact with numbers
References + comparison table vs 5 existing systems
decks.first_3_slides: Title, named product with feature bullets plus architecture, then a very large tech stack.
decks.architecture_visual: Icon-based client -> API -> DB -> modules diagram; plus a logo grid (React, FastAPI, Postgres, Kafka-style tools, K8s, AWS).
decks.numbers: Quantified claims: 70-90% reduction in rockfall incidents, 15-60 min early warning, $2-5M annual savings per large mine (no sources on slide).
decks.stood_out: Only SIH deck here with (a) a competitor feature-comparison table with ticks/crosses against 5 named products, (b) a business-model hint (subscription/tiered pricing), (c) numeric impact claims. Closest to MalanHack's benchmarking and revenue asks, but numbers are uncited and text is too dense.

decks.title: TransitMind (Team Niyati)
decks.event: SIH 2025, Smart Automation and Transportation (SIH25081, Kochi Metro)
slide_order: Proposed solution + detailed explanation + innovation, with data-sources -> engine -> outputs diagram
Technical approach: 5-step methodology + full pipeline diagram + logos
Impact and benefits with outcome diagram
References (named KPIs, docs, papers, Singapore MRT benchmark)
decks.first_3_slides: Title, solution with 'explainable ranked list' as the outcome, then a numbered methodology with architecture.
decks.architecture_visual: Left-to-right 3-column swimlane: data sources -> central engine -> outputs (list, dashboard, alerts), plus a full pipeline with feedback loop.
decks.numbers: >99.5% punctuality target; scalability to 40+ trainsets; one international benchmark (Singapore MRT) in references.
decks.stood_out: Explainable-AI framing ('why this train is chosen') as the trust mechanism, and a cross-country reference. Both transfer directly to LienLine (explain why this amount is held).

decks.title: IndiaGWanalytics.in (Team Zero++)
decks.event: SIH 2020, Disaster Management and Water Resources (DM84, CGWB)
slide_order: Problem statement + solution name + video link
Groundwater crisis in India (stat bullets + before/after satellite images of Chennai 2018 vs 2019)
Solution architecture mind-map + use cases + data collection
Solution walkthrough (two phone mockups with annotated flow)
Technology stack + features and future scope

decks.architecture_visual: Colour-coded hub-and-spoke map from the central 'Data Analysis' node to Visualization / Query / Reports / Extra features, with sample outputs on each spoke.

decks.demo_screenshots: Yes: annotated phone screens with callouts, plus an explicit demo video link on slide 2.
decks.stood_out: Best problem slide in the set: before/after satellite imagery plus red-highlighted numbers. Demo video linked on slide 2 and annotated screenshots mid-deck.

decks.title: KnitKraft (Team Vizion)
decks.event: SIH 2023, Agriculture and Textiles (SIH1309, Ministry of Textiles)
slide_order: Welcome / value props A-E beside phone mockup
Business model (escrow payments, QC fee, reverse bidding)

decks.architecture_visual: Role tree (not technical architecture); the 'architecture' is the UI itself.
decks.demo_screenshots: Yes: 8 dark-UI phone screens in numbered pairs with one-line annotations. Most polished UI/demo deck here.

decks.rank: Labelled 'Winner' in archive (unverified); team/institute fields were blank

decks.title: SIH 2026 Winning Playbook (TechDoodles), pitch-structure guidance
decks.event: SIH 2026 preparation guide (not a team deck)
decks.demo_screenshots: Advises a backup demo video recorded locally.

decks.title: Sequoia business-plan / pitch template
decks.rank: N/A, template widely used by winners
decks.first_3_slides: Purpose sentence, then problem (current handling + gaps), then solution (key insight).
decks.stood_out: Its 'Why now' slide is the one most hackathon decks omit. LienLine has a strong why-now (regulation, rising cyber-fraud, mule accounts, bank liability) and should use it.

decks.title: Colosseum / DePitch hackathon slide-by-slide guide (examples: Surf Cache, Nomu, Spend, CFL, Loot Go)
decks.event: Colosseum (Solana) hackathon winners, as analysed in a public skill repo
decks.rank: Winner decks as described by the repo author (secondary source, decks not opened)
slide_order: Demo (20-30 s, one flow, never last)
Market (user-intersection with numbers, not TAM triangle)
decks.first_3_slides: Product + one-liner; one problem with a number and an image; one-sentence value proposition.
decks.architecture_visual: Not emphasised; simple diagram preferred over busy UI.
decks.numbers: Two or three side-by-side numbers, comparison to benchmark ('50% D7 retention, 10x mobile game average'), Venn intersections to size a market.
decks.demo_screenshots: Demo slide after features and before market.
decks.stood_out: Concrete rules: no round unsourced numbers, no vanity metrics, no 5-year ARR in hackathon decks, dated roadmap, team slide led by one proven achievement.

decks.title: Investor-advice compilation (YC Hale/Ralston/Seibel, Hoffman, a16z, DocSend) with Airbnb, Uber, LinkedIn, Coinbase, Square patterns
decks.event: Benchmark guidance (structure only); decks not opened
slide_order: Cover tagline under 10 words (Airbnb: 'Book rooms with locals, rather than hotels')
Business model (one sentence of take-rate math)
decks.architecture_visual: Simple diagram over busy UI for live pitches.
decks.numbers: Funnel of three numbers; momentum rates; label axes; no cumulative charts.
decks.text_density_words_per_slide: Presented decks <= ~7 words/slide (Hale, Ralston); send-ahead decks readable standalone
decks.demo_screenshots: Show, do not describe; real screenshots for send-ahead decks.
decks.stood_out: DocSend data cited there: investors read a deck in ~2.5 min; successful pre-seed decks averaged 16 slides vs 19 for failures; competition and financial sections earn the most dwell time. Secondary source, verify before quoting.

recommended_order.note: 15 slides for the Round 1 PDF. It is read, not presented, so each slide must work alone (title as the claim, readable body). Every MalanHack pillar gets a named slide. The same deck is cut to ~10 slides for the Round 2 10-minute pitch (drop 3, 8, 12-ish detail slides into appendix) and an appendix serves the Round 3 Pune founder. Numbers in square brackets are placeholders to be sourced and cited; do not publish uncited figures.

slides.title: LienLine: hold the disputed amount, not the whole account
slides.purpose: Cover with one-liner under 10 words, product name, a single hook number (e.g. victims/accounts frozen) with source in footer.

slides.title: A fraud complaint freezes an entire account today
slides.purpose: One victim/innocent-account-holder story plus 2-3 big-number tiles (fraud losses, frozen accounts, complaints), each with source.

slides.title: Root cause: banks cannot tell how much of the money is traceable
slides.purpose: Before/after: current freeze-everything flow vs the amount-level lien flow; show who loses (innocent holders, banks facing court and RBI exposure, victims recovering too little).

slides.title: LienLine recommends a lien amount with evidence
slides.purpose: One-sentence solution, three benefit bullets, a one-line example (Rs X flagged, Rs Y traceable, hold Rs Y, release the rest).

slides.title: One case, end to end
slides.purpose: Annotated screenshot/mock of the working demo (case in, trail graph, recommended hold, explanation). Early demo slide.

slides.title: Five specialised agents turn a complaint into a defensible hold
slides.purpose: Architecture as a left-to-right flow with icons: inputs -> agents -> decision -> bank action/audit log. Label each agent in 5 words.

slides.title: How the amount is computed, and why it can be trusted
slides.purpose: Decision logic, evidence trace, confidence, human-in-the-loop sign-off, audit trail, false-positive handling, data privacy (DPDP). Show one worked calculation.

slides.title: Why now
slides.purpose: Regulatory and operational trigger(s) with citations; rising volume; mule-account pressure on banks. [verify each citation]

slides.title: Other countries already hold less than everything
slides.purpose: Benchmark table: 4-6 countries/regimes x (what is held, who decides, time limit, redress, tech used) with a citation per cell and a final 'India gap' row.

slides.title: Market: bottom-up from banks x cases x value
slides.purpose: Three-number funnel (banks/branches -> cases per year -> price per case = revenue pool), not a TAM triangle; state assumptions and sources.

slides.title: One revenue model
slides.purpose: One sentence of pricing math (per-case or per-bank subscription), unit economics, payback; one customer segment first.

slides.title: What it costs to build and take to market
slides.purpose: Three-column table: tech stack/infra, R&D (people, model/eval, compliance), GTM (pilot, sales, integration) with year-1 amounts and assumptions.

slides.title: Validation and how we compare
slides.purpose: Honest evidence (synthetic or pilot evaluation, accuracy vs baseline, precision of traceable amount) plus a 2x2 or short comparison vs existing bank fraud tools. No fake traction.

slides.title: Risks and how we handle them; roadmap
slides.purpose: Risk -> mitigation pairs (false lien, data access, regulator acceptance, model drift) and a dated 3-4 quarter roadmap, one milestone each.

slides.title: The ask and next steps
slides.purpose: What we want (pilot bank, data access, mentor/intro), what it unlocks by which date, team with one proven achievement, contact. End on the ask, not 'Thank you'.

recommended_order.round_2_cut: 10-minute pitch: slides 1,2,3,4,5,6,9,10-12 merged into one 'business' slide,14-15 merged. Open on the victim story, demo within the first 3 minutes.
recommended_order.round_3_pune_founder: Add an appendix aimed at a small security/compliance software vendor: integration surface (APIs, on-prem option), partner/white-label model, compliance checklist, what you need from them (distribution, domain review). Lead with how LienLine plugs into their product, not with market size.

design_rules: 1. One message per slide. Test: it must be summarisable in one sentence; if not, split it. SIH 'every slide answers one clear question' and Sequoia/YC both say this.

2. Write the title as the claim, not a label. 'A fraud complaint freezes an entire account today' not 'Problem'. Reading only the titles in order should make the whole argument. Most SIH decks fail this (Problem, Feasibility, Impact labels).

3. Big number plus source. Each stat is a tile with a large figure, a 5-word caption and a footer citation (publisher, year). Winning-pattern from Zero++ (red highlighted stats) and Colosseum (no unsourced round numbers). Never cumulative charts or vanity metrics.

4. Before/after visual for the core idea. A split panel: full freeze (red, all funds blocked) vs LienLine lien (only the traceable amount held, remainder released). It carries the problem and solution in one glance.

5. Architecture as a left-to-right flow with icons, 5-7 nodes, one verb per arrow, agent names with a 5-word role, plus the output. Fix the common SIH flaw of tiny text (Cannon Crew, TransitMind): minimum ~12 pt at PDF size. Show a real output next to the pipeline as GeoGuards did.
6. Put a demo screenshot early (slide 4-5) with numbered annotations and a one-line caption, as KnitKraft and Zero++ did. Link a short demo video on the cover or slide 5.

7. Benchmarking and cost slides are tables, not paragraphs: consistent columns, one citation per row, a bolded 'India gap' or 'our choice' row. Tech Pioneers' comparison table is the SIH precedent; the rest of the SIH set lacks this, so this is where we beat them.

8. Keep text light but self-sufficient, because Round 1 is read: 40-90 words per slide, bold the lead phrase of each bullet, no paragraphs, 3 bullets max. Use the SIH-winning density (KnitKraft ~25-100, GeoGuards ~50-110) not Tech Pioneers' 300.

9. Show validation honestly and pair every risk with a mitigation (greenSort, Cannon Crew, Niyati). Label synthetic data as synthetic; do not claim traction we do not have. Explainability ('why this amount') is the trust device (TransitMind).

10. End on the ask and next steps tied to a milestone, plus one consistent visual system: 2 colours + 1 accent, one icon set, one font pair, same title position on every slide, citations in the same footer style, brand mark small. Include a references slide or footer list.
mistakes: 1. Problem without evidence: prose problem statements with no number, source or visual (AlgoAllies, Innovators). Winners with strong problem slides use a stat plus an image (Zero++ satellite before/after).
2. Label titles and walls of text instead of claim titles and one idea per slide; 250-300 word slides (Tech Pioneers) that no judge reads in 2-3 minutes.
3. Unreadable architecture: tiny boxes and logo walls with no flow, or a stack list with no reasoning. Winners show a flow with data in, decision, and output, and say why each tool was chosen.

4. Skipping business pillars: no market size, cost, revenue or competitor comparison (most SIH decks), unsourced impact claims ('70-90% reduction'), top-down TAM, or multiple revenue models. Competition and financial slides get the most investor dwell time (secondary DocSend data).

5. Hiding the demo and ending weakly: no screenshot or video link, demo placed last, risks listed with no mitigation, no why-now, 'We have no competition', and a closing 'Thank you' slide rather than the ask.
sources: https://github.com/midovislam/awesome-pitch-decks (index of Airbnb/Uber/etc. decks on Google Drive; not opened)
